# glyospalettes

Color palettes for R and ggplot2 based on the named colorways of the
[Glyos](https://www.onelldesign.com/) toy system: Onell Design’s own
Glyos line plus the Glyos-compatible lines from partner companies such
as TheGodBeast (Kabuto Mushi), Spy Monkey Creations (Weaponeers of
Monkaa, Battle Tribes), Toyfinity (Robo Force, Zeroids, Manglors), the
Four Horsemen (Outer Space Men) and a dozen more. It works the same way
as packages like `wesanderson`: pick a colorway by name, get a vector of
hex colors, or drop a scale straight into a ggplot.

glyospalettes is a fan project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by
any of the companies whose colorways it describes. Hex values are
approximations curated from product photography; see “How the palettes
were made” below.

## Browse online

Every palette, with its colors, reference photo and provenance, is
browsable and filterable at
<https://bmaitner.github.io/glyospalettes/articles/browse.html>. Each
card has a **Suggest a change** link that opens a prefilled GitHub issue
where you can propose different colors or attach a cleaner photograph.

## Installation

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("bmaitner/glyospalettes")
```

## Usage

``` r

library(glyospalettes)

# which companies are covered, and how many palettes each has
glyos_companies()
table(glyos_colorways$company)

# palette names, optionally for one company or product line
glyos_palette_names()
glyos_palette_names(company = "TheGodBeast")
glyos_palette_names(line = "Battle Tribes")

# the colors of one colorway (prints the swatches and the hex codes)
glyos_palette("spectre")
#> Glyos colorway 'spectre' (4 colours)
#> Onell Design / Glyos: Spectre
#> #EEFADA #BCC99B #9EB49A #5FC3A8

# first three colors, a 12-step gradient, or the same gradient dark-to-light
glyos_palette("glyaxia", 3)
glyos_palette("hades", 12, type = "continuous")
glyos_palette("hades", 12, type = "continuous", sort = TRUE)

# swatches with hex codes, for one company at a time
glyos_show_palettes(company = "Onell Design")
glyos_show_palettes(company = "Spy Monkey Creations", ncol = 2)
```

![Onell Design palettes](reference/figures/palettes-onell.png)

Onell Design palettes

### ggplot2

[`scale_colour_glyos()`](https://bmaitner.github.io/glyospalettes/reference/scale_glyos.md)
and
[`scale_fill_glyos()`](https://bmaitner.github.io/glyospalettes/reference/scale_glyos.md)
build a discrete scale by default, or a continuous gradient with
`discrete = FALSE`. The explicit `_d` and `_c` variants and the American
`scale_color_*` spellings are also exported. `sort = TRUE` on a
continuous scale orders the palette from darkest to lightest first.

``` r

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy, colour = drv)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_colour_glyos("glyaxia")

ggplot(diamonds, aes(cut, fill = cut)) +
  geom_bar() +
  scale_fill_glyos("rf_vanguard")

ggplot(faithfuld, aes(waiting, eruptions, fill = density)) +
  geom_raster() +
  scale_fill_glyos_c("cosmic_wave", sort = TRUE)

ggplot(economics_long, aes(date, value01, colour = variable)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_colour_glyos("imperium")
```

![Example ggplot2 scales](reference/figures/examples.png)

Example ggplot2 scales

Set `reverse = TRUE` to flip a palette. If a discrete variable has more
levels than a palette has colors, the palette is interpolated so every
level still gets a color, at some cost to legibility.

### Finding a palette that works for a plot

Most colorways were designed to look good on a toy, not on a chart.
[`glyos_find_palettes()`](https://bmaitner.github.io/glyospalettes/reference/glyos_find_palettes.md)
shortlists the ones whose colors hold up for a given job, judged from
the colors themselves:

``` r

glyos_find_palettes("categorical")   # every pair of colours clearly distinct
glyos_find_palettes("colorblind")    # still distinct under simulated CVD
glyos_find_palettes("sequential")    # one hue, wide lightness range
glyos_find_palettes("diverging")     # two hues with a light colour between

# restrict to a company, or see the shortlist as swatches
glyos_find_palettes("colorblind", company = "Onell Design")
glyos_show_palettes(use = "colorblind", ncol = 3)
```

![Colorblind-friendly
shortlist](reference/figures/palettes-colorblind.png)

Colorblind-friendly shortlist

The judgments come from
[`glyos_palette_stats()`](https://bmaitner.github.io/glyospalettes/reference/glyos_palette_stats.md),
which reports the smallest pairwise distance between colors in CIE Lab,
the same after simulating deuteranopia, protanopia and tritanopia, the
lightness range, and the hue spread. The thresholds are simple
heuristics, so treat the result as a shortlist to look at rather than a
guarantee.

### Colorway background

`glyos_colorways` is a data frame with one row per palette: the company
and product line, the colorway name as the manufacturer uses it, the
year and wave of the reference release where known, a description of the
colors, and a link to the reference figure in the Official Glyos
Database (Onell) or the Glyos Wiki (partners).

``` r

t(glyos_colorways[glyos_colorways$palette == "kabuto_infection", ])
#> palette          "kabuto_infection"
#> company          "TheGodBeast"
#> line             "Kabuto Mushi"
#> colorway         "Infection"
#> year             "2014"
#> wave             NA
#> n_colours        "3"
#> description      "Clear red plastic."
#> reference_figure "Infection Kabuto Mushi"
#> source           "https://glyos.fandom.com/wiki/Infection_Kabuto_Mushi"
#> image            "https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/glyos/images/..."
```

The `image` column is a direct link to the photograph each palette was
sampled from, which is what the online browser shows.

## Coverage

| Company | Line(s) | Palettes | Prefix |
|----|----|----|----|
| Onell Design | Glyos | 45 | none, e.g. `spectre`, `glyaxia` |
| TheGodBeast | Kabuto Mushi | 10 | `kabuto_` |
| Spy Monkey Creations | Weaponeers of Monkaa, Battle Tribes | 18 | `wom_`, `bt_` |
| Toyfinity | Robo Force, Mordles, Zeroids, Manglors | 12 | `rf_`, `mordles_`, `zeroids_`, `manglors_` |
| Four Horsemen Studio | Outer Space Men, Power Lords | 12 | `osm_`, `powerlords_` |
| Toy Pizza | Knights of the Slice | 10 | `kots_` |
| Rocom Toys | Mighty Maniax | 10 | `maniax_` |
| Bio-Masters Design | Bio-Masters | 8 | `biomass_` |
| Rawshark Studio | Callgrim | 10 | `callgrim_`, `order_` |
| ManOrMonster? Studios | Warlords of Wor | 10 | `wor_` |
| NiStuff | Outlander | 10 | `outlander_` |
| Nemo’s Factory | A/V Robot | 8 | `avrobot_` |
| Cappy Space | Cappy Space | 8 | `cappy_` |
| Banimon | Banimon | 6 | `banimon_` |
| Culture Pirates | Bit Figs | 5 | `bitfigs_` |
| October Toys | Skeleton Warriors, Breaker Buildman | 4 | none |
| Zullbeasts | Zullbeasts | 4 | none |
| Spaced Out Design | Spaced Out, Rise of Acris | 3 | none |

Every partner company’s palettes are drawn in
`man/figures/palettes-<company>.png`; the Onell set is shown above. The
Onell palettes cover the classic colorways (Standard, Reverse, Spectre,
Hades Force, Infection, Neo Phase, Glyaxia, Gatekeeper, Stealth,
Classified and so on) plus the named division and faction waves. Partner
palettes are named after a representative figure or edition in that
line.

## How the palettes were made

There is no published set of hex values for Glyos colorways, so these
are approximations built in three steps:

1.  Each colorway was matched to a representative figure. For Onell
    Design that is an entry in the [Official Glyos
    Database](https://database.glyos.com/), preferring a Pheyden or
    Glyan so that body, secondary and paint colors are all visible. For
    partner companies it is the figure’s page on the [Glyos
    Wiki](https://glyos.fandom.com/).
2.  The dominant colors of that figure’s lead photograph were extracted
    with k-means clustering, after masking out pixels that match the
    photo’s border colors so that studio backgrounds, rocks and
    tabletops do not leak into the palette.
3.  The clusters were reconciled by eye against the manufacturer’s own
    color descriptions where they exist, chiefly the Onell drop
    announcements on the [Glyos Transmission Web
    Log](https://onelldesign.blogspot.com/) (for example “Pappysoup
    Green/Olive Green with light green visors and white tampo”, or “Cool
    Gray 1C + Cool Gray 8C + Cool Gray 10C detail lines” for Zorennor)
    and the wiki’s release lists, and ordered so the first few colors in
    each palette are the most distinct.

Each palette contains only plastic and paint colors, so a colorway cast
in a single clear plastic yields a short palette of that hue’s
highlight, mid-tone and shadow, and a two-color colorway such as Kabuto
Mushi Radioactive is just two colors. Palettes range from 2 to 6 colors.
Clear, glow-in-the-dark, metallic and pearlescent plastics do not reduce
to a single flat color; those palettes reflect how the plastic
photographs rather than the pigment itself. Partner-company photographs
vary more in lighting and background than Onell’s, so expect those
palettes to be rougher. Corrections are welcome, ideally with a
photograph or a manufacturer color description to back them up. Use the
[palette
browser](https://bmaitner.github.io/glyospalettes/articles/browse.html)
to open a prefilled issue for a specific palette, or pick a form from
the [issue
templates](https://github.com/bmaitner/glyospalettes/issues/new/choose):
suggest a palette change, submit a cleaner reference photo (plain
background, neutral light), or propose a new colorway.
[`glyos_show_palettes()`](https://bmaitner.github.io/glyospalettes/reference/glyos_show_palettes.md)
prints the hex codes under each swatch to make reporting easy.

## Trademarks

Glyos, Pheyden and the Onell Design colorway names belong to Onell
Design. Kabuto Mushi, Weaponeers of Monkaa, Battle Tribes, Robo Force,
Zeroids, Manglors, Mordles, Outer Space Men, Power Lords, Knights of the
Slice, Mighty Maniax, Bio-Masters, Callgrim, Warlords of Wor, Outlander,
A/V Robot, Bit Figs, Banimon, Skeleton Warriors and Zullbeasts belong to
their respective companies. This package only records approximate color
values and uses the names to refer to them.

  : Get colors from a Glyos colorway

  : List the available Glyos palettes

  : List the companies with palettes in glyospalettes

  : Display Glyos palettes
